3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("nortest", "ggplot2"))
library(nortest)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# === 01 · Distribution & normality ===
xv <- na.omit(d[["exam_score"]]); nv <- length(xv)
if (nv >= 3 && nv <= 5000) print(shapiro.test(xv)) else cat("Shapiro-Wilk: n outside [3, 5000]\n")
if (nv >= 5) print(nortest::lillie.test(xv)) else cat("Lilliefors: n too small (need n >= 5)\n")
print(ggplot(d, aes(exam_score)) + geom_histogram(bins = max(5L, min(30L, ceiling(log2(length(na.omit(d[["exam_score"]]))) + 1)))) + labs(x = "exam_score", y = "Count"))
print(ggplot(d, aes(sample = exam_score)) + stat_qq() + stat_qq_line() + labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles"))
xv <- na.omit(d[["absences"]]); nv <- length(xv)
if (nv >= 3 && nv <= 5000) print(shapiro.test(xv)) else cat("Shapiro-Wilk: n outside [3, 5000]\n")
if (nv >= 5) print(nortest::lillie.test(xv)) else cat("Lilliefors: n too small (need n >= 5)\n")
print(ggplot(d, aes(absences)) + geom_histogram(bins = max(5L, min(30L, ceiling(log2(length(na.omit(d[["absences"]]))) + 1)))) + labs(x = "absences", y = "Count"))
print(ggplot(d, aes(sample = absences)) + stat_qq() + stat_qq_line() + labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles"))

\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}

\usepackage{booktabs,graphicx,siunitx}

\begin{document}

\section{Distribution \& normality}

\begin{tabular}{lllllll}
\toprule
Variable & Test & Statistic & N & p & Skew & Kurtosis (excess) \\
\midrule
exam\_score & Shapiro-Wilk & W 0.99 & 240 & .158 & $-$0.18 & $-$0.53 \\
exam\_score & K--S (Lilliefors) & D 0.04 & 240 & .608 & $-$0.18 & $-$0.53 \\
absences & Shapiro-Wilk & W 0.86 & 240 & $<$.001 & 1.50 & 2.43 \\
absences & K--S (Lilliefors) & D 0.17 & 240 & $<$.001 & 1.50 & 2.43 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\includegraphics{figures/01_distribution-normality/figure_histogram_exam_score.png}

\includegraphics{figures/01_distribution-normality/figure_qq_exam_score.png}

\includegraphics{figures/01_distribution-normality/figure_histogram_absences.png}

\includegraphics{figures/01_distribution-normality/figure_qq_absences.png}

A small p (below .05) suggests the data depart from normality. With large samples these tests over-flag trivial deviations; with small samples they have low power, so a p $>$ .05 does not prove normality - it only means no departure was detected. Either way, judge normality mainly from the Q--Q plot - points hugging the diagonal indicate normality.

exam\_score: Normality was assessed with the Shapiro-Wilk test, W = .99, p = .158. absences: Normality was assessed with the Shapiro-Wilk test, W = .86, p $<$ .001.

Statistical basis: Shapiro-Wilk test for normality (3-5000 cases) (Shapiro, S. S., Wilk, M. B. (1965). "An analysis of variance test for normality (complete samples)." Biometrika, 52(3/4), 591-611.); Additional normality tests (Lilliefors and related) (Gross J, Ligges U (2015). nortest: Tests for Normality. R package.).

\end{document}

Harness README
# 03 · Distribution & normality

**Question:** is a variable normally distributed?

**Scenario:** Campus study: exam score looks normal, but absences is right-skewed.

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** Shapiro-Wilk + Kolmogorov–Smirnov; histogram + Q–Q per variable

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `exam_score` | variable |
| `absences` | variable |
